transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can’t keep my thoughts organized anymore, and it’s getting hard to make even simple decisions at work. It's gotten to the point where I'm making mistakes with my clients' schedules, and my supervisor suggested I see someone because my mind just feels so scattered.
Have you been feeling down or unable to enjoy things most days, or did these problems start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yes, lately I've been feeling this heavy, empty sadness, like a gray cloud is constantly sitting on my chest. This latest low period started about a month ago, right after my mom's doctor in Mexico told us her diabetes had gotten much worse. Trying to handle her care and the extra medical expenses has just been incredibly stressful.

Since your mother’s health worsened, have you been worrying uncontrollably about many different things most days, or is it mainly a deep sadness and loss of interest that’s been most prominent? Have these feelings been present nearly every day for at least two weeks?

While I do worry a lot at night about my mom's health, the most prominent feeling has been this heavy, empty sadness where I just feel completely hollow and defeated. This has been happening nearly every day for about a month now, so it's definitely been longer than two weeks.

During this past month, have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even when you have time for them? Or does it feel more like your sadness is mainly tied to the stress about your mother’s illness and finances?

I haven't had any time for my usual hobbies like car restoration or board-game nights lately because of my demanding schedule. But this sadness feels like more than just stress about my mom—it's this heavy, empty, hollow feeling that is constantly there and makes me tear up for no clear reason.

Over the past month, have you also had other depression symptoms like trouble sleeping, changes in appetite or weight, low energy, feeling worthless or guilty, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? Or does it mostly feel like sadness related to the stress of your mother’s illness?

Yes, I barely sleep because I'm either lying awake worrying or waking up in a panic, which leaves me so exhausted that just showering wipes me out. I also carry this heavy guilt that I'm failing my family and clients, and sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up.
Have you had any experiences like hearing voices or strongly believing things others say aren’t true, and are you still able to manage basic daily tasks like eating, bathing, and getting to work?

No, I don't hear voices or have any unusual beliefs like that. But managing daily life has become incredibly hard, and even basic things like showering and getting dressed completely wipe me out. My work is suffering to the point where I've had clients reassigned, and my wife has had to take over managing our household bills because I just can't keep up.
When you think it would be easier if you didn’t wake up, have you had any thoughts of killing yourself, made a plan, or done anything to prepare? Are you safe right now?

I've definitely had those thoughts where I feel like everyone would be better off without me because I keep screwing things up, or that it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up. But I want to be clear that I haven't made any plans or taken any steps to hurt myself, and I am absolutely safe right now.

Even when you do get a chance to do something you usually enjoy, like car restoration or board-game nights, does it still feel hard to enjoy or care about it? Or do you think you would enjoy it normally if you had the time?
I haven't really had the time or energy to try those things lately with everything going on. Because of that, I'm not completely sure if I would still enjoy them right now or not.

When something good happens or you get a brief break from dealing with your mom’s illness, does your mood lift noticeably, or do you still feel deeply depressed no matter what? Does the sadness feel mostly tied to that stress, or has it taken on a life of its own?

Even when I get a break or spend time with my wife, my mood doesn't lift and I still feel that heavy, hollow sadness. While the stress with my mom started all of this, the sadness has definitely taken on a life of its own now and doesn't just go away when things quiet down.
Even when you do make yourself start something you used to enjoy, do you still get little or no pleasure from it? Can you think of a recent example?

I honestly haven't even tried to start any of my hobbies lately because I just don't have the time or the energy. Because of that, I don't really have a recent example to share, and I'm not sure how I would feel doing them right now.
Over the past month, have you noticed a clear change in your appetite or weight, either eating much less or much more than usual? If yes, about how much has your weight changed?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight recently. My mind has been so focused on my mother's health and all the stress at work that I haven't paid much attention to how much I'm eating.
Compared with what’s happening with your mother, does your depression feel clearly more intense than you would expect from that stress alone? Or does it feel about in proportion to the situation?
I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about it that way. Everything just feels incredibly overwhelming and hard to sort through right now, so it's difficult to tell.

In the past month, if you actually had a chance to do something you usually enjoy, do you think you would still feel little or no pleasure from it? Or do you think you’d enjoy it normally and that the problem is mostly not having time because of your mother’s illness?

It is really a combination of both. I have virtually no time for my usual hobbies like car restoration or board game nights because of my mother's care and my extra work shifts. But even if I did have a free moment, I feel so hollow, completely exhausted, and weighed down by sadness lately that I don't think I would be able to find any real enjoyment in them right now.
